title: feat: mint strict flag in payment request
body:
# Fixes: #[issue]

## Description

Adds mintsStrict (ms) field to PaymentRequest as specified in NUT-18 and NUT-26 pull request: https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/380.

When ms is absent or true (default), the recipient MUST reject payments from mints not in the mint list. When ms is false, the mint list is a suggestion for the payer only.

---

## Changes

- Add ms?: boolean to RawPaymentRequest type
- Add mintsStrict?: boolean to PaymentRequest constructor and all encode/decode paths (toRawRequest, toEncodedCreqB, fromRawRequest, fromEncodedRequest)
- Add TLV tag 0x09 (TAG_MINT_STRICT) to DecodedTLVPaymentRequest type and encode/decode logic in tlv.ts

---

## Alignment & Discussion

- Was an issue opened prior to this PR? [No]
- Does this PR align with the current project direction and scope? [Yes]
- Link any relevant discussion or RFC: https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/380.

---

## Reviewer Notes

- Absence of ms is semantically equivalent to true (strict) — this matches the spec default and requires no migration of existing encoded requests
- mintsStrict is only serialized when explicitly set (!== undefined), so existing CBOR and TLV encodings are unchanged

---

title: fix(crypto): align NUT-29 batch quote signatures with amended spec

labels.name: nut hold
labels.description: This PR is held pending the merge of a new or updated NUT

body:
Implements: https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/375

## Summary

Aligns the mint-quote signature messages with the amended cashubtc/nuts#375, which splits the two cases:

- **NUT-20** (single mint quote) is reverted to its original, retro-compatible message (`quote || B_0 || … || B_(n-1)`, plain hex concatenation). Wire format unchanged.
- **NUT-29** (batch mint) gets its own domain-separated, length-framed message in a new `src/crypto/NUT29.ts` (`signBatchMintQuote` / `verifyBatchMintQuoteSignature`):

  ```
  msg_to_sign = DST || len32(quote) || quote
                || for each output: len32(amount) || amount || len32(B_) || B_
  ```

  where `DST = "Cashu_MintQuoteSig_v1"`, `len32(x)` is the 4-byte big-endian length of `x`, `amount` is the canonical minimal big-endian encoding (`0` → empty), and `B_` is the raw compressed point. The signature is a BIP340 Schnorr signature over the SHA-256 of that byte string.

The batch-mint path (`prepareBatchMint`) now signs with `signBatchMintQuote`; the single-quote path is untouched. Tests are pinned to the canonical vector in `tests/29-tests.md` (`msg_hash = 03dc68d6…`).

## Motivation

The batch message now commits to each output's amount as well as its blinded point, in order, so a locked-quote signature cannot be replayed against a reordered or re-valued output set — this closes the output-malleability gap that the earlier separator-only approach left open. The length framing makes field boundaries unambiguous across curves (33-byte secp256k1 / 48-byte BLS points) without relying on point self-delimitation. NUT-20 keeps its existing format to avoid a needless break for already-deployed mints.

This changes the bytes signed for NUT-29 batch authentication; mints must adopt the same construction (per cashubtc/nuts#375) to verify.
